issues.description: The problem statement explicitly says the framebuffer start is at a "global exportierte Speicherstelle display_start" (i.e. an exported/global symbol), but neither the template nor the solution declare display_start as a global/exported symbol (they only define it in .bss). This mismatch can confuse students who expect an explicitly exported/global symbol (for example when linking modules or following the wording).
issues.suggested_fix: Either declare the symbol as global in the template and solution (e.g. add a line 'global display_start' near the top of the .asm files) so the code matches the problem wording, or adjust the problem statement to remove/soften the wording about 'global exportierte' if the exercise is intended to be a single-file program. Adding 'global display_start' in the template (and solution) will preserve the educational intent while removing the visibility mismatch.
